rv.q: "You must hear me," implores a blind Vietnam veteran of his middle-aged, middle-American father. "It is only fraud that keeps us sane." This kind of urgency jolts through every vein of the New Group's throbbing revival of Sticks and Bones, David Rabe's seriously twisted 1971 satirical drama...

David Rabe's blistering Vietnam-era play Sticks and Bones -- currently playing in a galvanizing, brilliant revival... -- is one of those works that can crash and burn at the slightest misappropriation...One false move by any creators can easily tip the play into either silliness, or worse, indifference. Scott Elliott's expertly rendered production..
Watching the New Group's tough, horrifyingly funny revival of David Rabe's 'Sticks and Bones' is like entering an eerie time capsule.
This play, while intense, feels bald and dated more often than it does bold and razor-sharp.

tn.cat: Best Featured Actress in a Play

cn.t: Rabe's searing Vietnam-era satire receives a galvanizing revival, though critics find the nearly three-hour play feels dated and overlong. Strong performances and Elliott's expert direction mostly compensate for the work's uneven impact.

vs.sum: The John Golden Theatre offers good sightlines from most seats, though sound quality can vary, especially under the mezzanine. Seating comfort is typical of older theaters with tight legroom, but the venue maintains a pleasant ambiance overall. Facilities are adequate, though not exceptional.

acc.note: 5 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. No wheelchair-accessible restroom (use adjacent Schoenfeld).
